pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: mm: per-process reclaim These day, there are many platforms available in the embedded market and they are smarter than kernel which has very limited information about working set so they want to involve memory management more heavily like android's lowmemory killer and ashmem or recent many lowmemory notifier. One of the simple imagine scenario about userspace's intelligence is that platform can manage tasks as forground and background so it would be better to reclaim background's task pages for end-user's *responsibility* although it has frequent referenced pages. This patch adds new knob "reclaim under proc/<pid>/" so task manager can reclaim any target process anytime, anywhere. It could give another method to platform for using memory efficiently. It can avoid process killing for getting free memory, which was really terrible experience because I lost my best score of game I had ever after I switch the phone call while I enjoyed the game. Reclaim file-backed pages only. echo file > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim anonymous pages only. echo anon > /proc/PID/reclaim Reclaim all pages echo all > /proc/PID/reclaim BUG=chromium:973963 TEST=build/boot 4.4 Change-Id: I2f629f7a43289af114df27044b1d2af4a6e785bc Signed-off-by: Tim Murray <timmurray@google.com> Signed-off-by: Minchan Kim <minchan@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit e48b0dd9cc1fa572455434357f5678018b3458b9) modification for zone-lru list from 4.9 Signed-off-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org> [SR: fs/proc/base.c: add CONFIG_MMU ifdef guard for reclaim file] (cherry picked from commit 5e95f6a8aacad0289b1df3a6fbb1cfa4f99c6519 in android-msm-wahoo-4.4) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1733919 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Geffon <bgeffon@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: fix passing active page into shrink_page_list Currently, per-process reclaim calls shrink_page_list several times with zone loop. However, it's pointless that passing pages failed to reclaim in earlier trial. More severe problem is shrink_page_list can mark victim pages as PG_active so next trial of shrink_page_list with those PG_active page in the loop can warn like below. Remove the unncessary loop with zone iterator and just pass NULL as zone argument in shrink_page_list. The shrink_page_list doesn't rely on zone except writeback throttling logic in memory pressure. BACKPORT: mm: move lazily freed pages to inactive list MADV_FREE is a hint that it's okay to discard pages if there is memory pressure and we use reclaimers(ie, kswapd and direct reclaim) to free them so there is no value keeping them in the active anonymous LRU so this patch moves them to inactive LRU list's head. This means that MADV_FREE-ed pages which were living on the inactive list are reclaimed first because they are more likely to be cold rather than recently active pages. An arguable issue for the approach would be whether we should put the page to the head or tail of the inactive list. I chose head because the kernel cannot make sure it's really cold or warm for every MADV_FREE usecase but at least we know it's not *hot*, so landing of inactive head would be a comprimise for various usecases. This fixes suboptimal behavior of MADV_FREE when pages living on the active list will sit there for a long time even under memory pressure while the inactive list is reclaimed heavily. This basically breaks the whole purpose of using MADV_FREE to help the system to free memory which is might not be used. CHROMIUM: mm: perproc-reclaim: do not discarding file-backed pages With testing, I found sometime perproc-reclaim shows regression with more LMKD kill because LMKD still relies on the file-LRU size while perproc-reclaim could make the file-LRU smaller. This patch changes the policy of file-backed LRU shrinking. Instead of discarding pages of perprocess reclaim, just makes them easy-reclaimable pages, for instance, move active file pages to inactive, clear PG_referenced and pte access bits. With that, we could keep file-LRU bigger so that more change to hit in the cache while VM can shrink quickly when memory spike happens. shill: service: Add disconnecting state Prior to this change, Service had no disconnecting state. Since the Service Disconnect D-Bus call is officially supporting the semantics that a Disconnect only initiates a disconnect, there is the potential of a Connect being called on a Service that has not yet finished disconnecting. Introducing the disconnect Service state allows for this case to be clear both internally to shill and to clients. This change does *not* yet cause the disconnecting state to be used. Chrome currently has one case where receiving kStateDisconnect from Shill will hit a NOTREACHED, which should be changed after Chrome's system_api is uprev'd to include the change from "disconnect" -> "disconnecting". The Wilco EC is able to return telemetry information (such as temperature and fan state) via sysfs: You write a binary command to the sysfs file, the kernel driver performs some filtering on the command to ensure it is sane, and the EC returns the binary result, to be read from the same file. You must keep the file descriptor open between the read and write for the response to be kept. This test checks for end-to-end communication with the EC, and checks that the driver performs some basic filtering and sanity checks. Since the responses are variable and opaque binary data, it's impractical to actually check the values of the responses. See https://chromium.git.corp.google.com/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/ea0f6a09a7a993fc7c781fd8ca675b29c42d4719/drivers/platform/chrome/wilco_ec/telemetry.c for the kernel driver. shill: point ethernet_any to first available Ethernet service There are a set of assumptions that Chrome makes when applying service policies that aren't currently upheld with regards to the ethernet_any service (i.e. ethernet_any is not in the ServiceCompleteList, and the service path returned when ethernet_any is configured is not the same one returned after a device is plugged in). We address that in this change by pointing ethernet_any to the first available Ethernet service (dictated by the service sorting heuristic). The algorithm is as follows: when a new Ethernet service is created first check to see if there are currently any Ethernet services. If there aren't, simply assign the new Ethernet device to the existing ethernet_any service instead of instantiating a new one. This way, the service path remains the same if ConfigureServiceForProfile was called before a device was plugged in. If this device is removed at some point, point ethernet_any at the first Ethernet service in the list. This service will now act as the ethernet_any service. If, at some point, the last Ethernet device is unplugged, instead of destroying the service, convert it back to the generic ethernet_any service by removing the associated device and setting the storage identifier to "ethernet_any". TODO: if there are multiple Ethernet services and the default service changes, the GUID remains the same. Chrome may expect the GUID and service path to be consistent, so this will probably need to be corrected. BUG=chromium:949553,chromium:950067,chromium:988599 TEST=1) unittests 2) deployed to DUT, configured static IP, and did the following: a) plugged in eth0 b) plugged in eth1 c) removed eth0 d) removed eth1 Confirmed that ethernet_any pointed to the correct service at all steps and that static IP transferred between the two Ethernet services when it should. 3) ConfigureServiceForProfile still works and now returns the same service path. 4) network_VPNConnect no longer persists 10.9.8.2 IP Change-Id: Ib2f3c398cc188db2f307df68aeadbd80e9f65d98 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1580541 Tested-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthew Wang <matthewmwang@chromium.org>
